significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that "only a small subset of CoT tokens are 'load-bearing'" because their representations are "causally consumed by downstream layers," and that removing the remainder preserves answers; this is a form-(ii) causal claim establishing both a sparsity phenomenon and a mechanism for one behavior, rather than a transferable law. It would constrain explanations of CoT computation and support per-instance stopping more directly than token-budget approaches such as Snell et al.'s test-time-compute scaling and Muennighoff et al.'s s1 budget forcing, but it remains the topic's default separable-importance-plus-intervention template and does not predict a quantitative relationship across new models. Verified false is distinguishable and informative: it would show that answer-relevant computation is diffuse or that downstream readout cannot support the claimed pruning, although it would not rule out other efficiency mechanisms. In the topic-substitution check, replacing the sparse causal premise with generic "mechanistic efficient reasoning" would merit only the topic median, so the specific causal account raises this only modestly above 5.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "training-free inference-time controller" using a probe to "predict when the model has produced enough load-bearing content," which is ex ante because it triggers early answer generation before additional tokens and cost are incurred. This gives an action window useful to practitioners serving or gating reasoning models, not merely a post-hoc explanation for interpretability researchers. However, the claim concedes that the "probe may not transfer across models/datasets, requiring per-setting calibration," and it states no cross-model law predicting what load-bearing fraction or savings will be recovered after recalibration; the asserted scope is therefore strongest across CoT math and logic tasks, not architectures or modalities generally. The topic alone supplies neither this online predictor nor its lead time, so the topic-substitution check supports an above-median score, while limited transfer keeps it at the bottom of the 7–8 band.
